questions.text: Do you have a next-generation firewall (NGFW) deployed at your network perimeter?

options.text: Yes, with comprehensive IPS/IDS and application control

questions.recommendation: Deploy a next-generation firewall with intrusion prevention, deep packet inspection, and application-aware filtering to protect your network perimeter.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a modern firewall, your network perimeter is vulnerable to unauthorized access, malware, and sophisticated attacks that can bypass traditional packet filters.

questions.text: Do you use a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect public-facing web applications?
questions.recommendation: Implement a WAF for all public-facing web applications to protect against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, SQL injection, XSS, and other web-based attacks.
questions.riskExplanation: Web applications are common attack vectors. Without WAF protection, your applications are exposed to injection attacks, data breaches, and service disruptions.

questions.text: Do you conduct regular penetration testing of your external-facing infrastructure?
questions.recommendation: Schedule quarterly penetration tests by qualified security professionals to identify and remediate vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.
questions.riskExplanation: Without regular penetration testing, unknown vulnerabilities in your perimeter defenses may remain undetected until exploited by malicious actors.

questions.text: Do you have DDoS protection services in place?

options.text: Yes, with dedicated DDoS mitigation service

questions.recommendation: Implement a dedicated DDoS protection service with traffic scrubbing capabilities to ensure availability during volumetric attacks.
questions.riskExplanation: DDoS attacks can cause significant downtime and revenue loss. Basic ISP protection is often insufficient against sophisticated, multi-vector attacks.

questions.text: Is your internal network segmented to separate critical systems from general traffic?

options.text: Yes, with multiple security zones and strict controls

questions.recommendation: Implement network segmentation using VLANs, subnets, and firewall rules to isolate critical systems and limit lateral movement by attackers.
questions.riskExplanation: Flat networks allow attackers to move freely once they gain initial access. Segmentation contains breaches and protects critical assets.

questions.text: Do you monitor network traffic for security anomalies and intrusions?

options.text: Yes, with SIEM and automated alerting

questions.recommendation: Deploy a SIEM solution with network traffic analysis, anomaly detection, and automated alerting to identify suspicious activities in real-time.
questions.riskExplanation: Without network monitoring, security incidents may go undetected for extended periods, allowing attackers to exfiltrate data or cause damage.

questions.text: Do you enforce network access control (NAC) for devices connecting to your network?
questions.recommendation: Implement 802.1X authentication with NAC to ensure only authorized and compliant devices can access network resources.
questions.riskExplanation: Unauthorized devices on your network can introduce malware, bypass security controls, and provide attackers with entry points.

questions.text: Do you use VPN with multi-factor authentication for remote access?

options.text: Yes, MFA required for all remote users
Yes, MFA optional or for some users

questions.recommendation: Enforce MFA for all VPN connections and consider implementing Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) for more secure remote access.
questions.riskExplanation: VPN credentials are frequently targeted. Without MFA, compromised credentials allow attackers full access to your internal network.

answer.optionText: Yes, MFA optional or for some users

questions.text: Do you have endpoint detection and response (EDR) deployed on all corporate devices?

options.text: Yes, on all devices with centralized management

questions.recommendation: Deploy EDR solutions across all endpoints to detect, investigate, and respond to threats in real-time with automated containment capabilities.
questions.riskExplanation: Endpoints are primary attack vectors. Without EDR, malware and advanced threats can spread undetected across your organization.

answer.optionText: Yes, on all devices with centralized management

questions.text: Are all endpoints kept up-to-date with security patches within a defined timeframe?
questions.recommendation: Implement automated patch management with defined SLAs (e.g., critical patches within 48 hours, all patches within 7 days) to reduce vulnerability exposure.
questions.riskExplanation: Unpatched vulnerabilities are among the most common exploitation methods. Delays in patching increase your risk significantly.

questions.text: Do you enforce full-disk encryption on all corporate laptops and mobile devices?
questions.recommendation: Mandate full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or equivalent) on all corporate devices to protect data at rest in case of theft or loss.
questions.riskExplanation: Unencrypted devices expose sensitive data if lost or stolen. Encryption is a fundamental protection for data at rest.

questions.text: Do you have application whitelisting or allow-listing policies in place?
questions.recommendation: Implement application allow-listing to prevent execution of unauthorized software, reducing the attack surface for malware and unauthorized tools.
questions.riskExplanation: Without application control, users can install malicious or unauthorized software, increasing security risks and compliance issues.

questions.text: Do you conduct static application security testing (SAST) during development?
questions.recommendation: Integrate SAST tools into your CI/CD pipeline to automatically detect security vulnerabilities during the development process.
questions.riskExplanation: Security vulnerabilities introduced during development are expensive to fix later. SAST catches issues early in the lifecycle.

questions.text: Do you perform dynamic application security testing (DAST) on applications before production deployment?
questions.recommendation: Implement automated DAST scanning for all application releases to identify runtime vulnerabilities before they reach production.
questions.riskExplanation: Runtime vulnerabilities are only detectable when applications are running. DAST complements SAST by finding issues in deployed configurations.

questions.text: Do you use software composition analysis (SCA) to scan third-party dependencies?

options.text: Yes, automated scanning of all dependencies

questions.recommendation: Implement SCA tools to automatically scan all third-party dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and license compliance issues.
questions.riskExplanation: Third-party libraries often contain vulnerabilities. SCA helps you identify and update risky dependencies before they can be exploited.

questions.text: Do you have a secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) policy in place?
questions.recommendation: Develop and enforce a comprehensive SSDLC policy that includes security requirements, threat modeling, code reviews, and developer security training.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a structured SSDLC, security is often an afterthought, leading to vulnerabilities that could have been prevented through proper processes.

questions.text: Do you have a formal data classification policy (e.g., public, internal, confidential, restricted)?
questions.recommendation: Implement a data classification framework with automated labeling and enforce appropriate protection controls based on classification levels.
questions.riskExplanation: Without data classification, you cannot apply appropriate protection controls, leading to either over-protection of low-value data or under-protection of sensitive information.

questions.text: Do you encrypt sensitive data both at rest and in transit?

options.text: Yes, for at rest or transit only

questions.recommendation: Implement strong encryption (AES-256 for at rest, TLS 1.3 for transit) for all sensitive data, with proper key management practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Unencrypted data is vulnerable to interception and theft. Encryption is essential for protecting sensitive information in all states.

questions.text: Do you have regular data backup with tested recovery procedures?

options.text: Yes, automated with quarterly recovery tests
Yes, automated but no regular testing

questions.recommendation: Implement the 3-2-1 backup strategy (3 copies, 2 different media, 1 offsite) with regular recovery testing to ensure business continuity.
questions.riskExplanation: Without tested backups, data loss from ransomware, hardware failure, or human error can be catastrophic and unrecoverable.

answer.optionText: Yes, automated with quarterly recovery tests

questions.text: Do you implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls?

options.text: Yes, with endpoint and network DLP

questions.recommendation: Deploy comprehensive DLP solutions across endpoints, network, and cloud to prevent unauthorized transmission of sensitive data.
questions.riskExplanation: Data breaches often occur through accidental or malicious data exfiltration. DLP controls help prevent sensitive data from leaving your environment.

questions.text: Do you enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all admin accounts?

options.text: Yes, for all admin and privileged accounts

questions.recommendation: Enforce MFA using phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2, hardware keys) for all administrative and privileged accounts without exception.
questions.riskExplanation: Admin accounts are high-value targets. Without MFA, compromised credentials give attackers full control over your systems.

questions.text: Do you enforce MFA for all user accounts?

options.text: Yes, optional or for some users

questions.recommendation: Implement MFA for all user accounts, starting with passwordless authentication where possible, to dramatically reduce credential theft risks.
questions.riskExplanation: Password-based authentication is fundamentally weak. MFA is one of the most effective controls against account compromise.

questions.text: Do you follow the principle of least privilege for access rights?
questions.recommendation: Implement least privilege access with quarterly access reviews, automated provisioning/deprovisioning, and just-in-time access for privileged roles.
questions.riskExplanation: Excessive access rights increase the impact of compromised accounts. Regular reviews are essential to prevent privilege creep.

questions.text: Do you have a single sign-on (SSO) solution for cloud applications?
questions.recommendation: Deploy SSO with centralized identity management to improve security, simplify user management, and enable consistent access policies across applications.
questions.riskExplanation: Without SSO, users must manage multiple credentials, leading to password reuse and increased attack surface for credential theft.

questions.text: Do you have controlled physical access to your data centers and server rooms?

options.text: Yes, keycard or basic access control

questions.recommendation: Implement multi-factor physical access controls with audit logging for all data center and server room entries, including visitor management.
questions.riskExplanation: Unauthorized physical access can lead to equipment theft, data theft, and sabotage. Physical security is foundational to overall security.

answer.optionText: Yes, keycard or basic access control

questions.text: Do you have video surveillance monitoring critical areas?
questions.recommendation: Deploy video surveillance with adequate retention (90+ days) for all critical areas, with regular review procedures and secure storage.
questions.riskExplanation: Video surveillance deters physical attacks and provides forensic evidence for investigations. Without it, physical incidents are harder to investigate.

questions.text: Do you have visitor management procedures for all facilities?

options.text: Yes, with escort requirements and logging

questions.recommendation: Implement comprehensive visitor management including pre-registration, badge issuance, escort requirements, and exit confirmation.
questions.riskExplanation: Unmanaged visitors pose significant security risks. Formal procedures ensure accountability and prevent unauthorized access.

answer.optionText: Yes, with escort requirements and logging

questions.text: Do you have environmental controls (fire suppression, HVAC, UPS) for critical infrastructure?
questions.recommendation: Implement comprehensive environmental controls with monitoring, regular maintenance, and automated alerts for fire, temperature, humidity, and power.
questions.riskExplanation: Environmental failures (fire, flood, power loss) can cause catastrophic damage and extended downtime. Proper controls are essential for availability.

questions.text: Do you have documented security policies covering all major areas?
questions.recommendation: Develop and maintain a comprehensive set of security policies with annual reviews, including acceptance tracking and compliance monitoring.
questions.riskExplanation: Without clear policies, security practices are inconsistent and employees lack guidance on proper security behaviors.

questions.text: Do you provide regular security awareness training to all employees?
questions.recommendation: Implement quarterly security awareness training with phishing simulations, covering current threats and reinforcing security best practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Employees are often the weakest link. Regular training significantly reduces the risk of phishing, social engineering, and human error.

questions.text: Do you have an incident response plan that is regularly tested?
questions.recommendation: Develop a comprehensive incident response plan with defined roles, playbooks, and conduct annual tabletop exercises to test and improve response capabilities.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a tested incident response plan, security incidents will be handled chaotically, increasing damage and recovery time.

questions.text: Do you conduct regular security compliance audits or assessments?
questions.recommendation: Schedule annual security assessments with qualified auditors to validate compliance with policies, regulations, and industry best practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Without regular audits, security gaps may go undetected, and you may fail to identify non-compliance with regulatory requirements.

questions.riskExplanation: Excessive access rights increase the impact of compromised accounts. Regular reviews are essential to prevent privilege creep.

questions.text: Do you have a single sign-on (SSO) solution for cloud applications?
questions.recommendation: Deploy SSO with centralized identity management to improve security, simplify user management, and enable consistent access policies across applications.
questions.riskExplanation: Without SSO, users must manage multiple credentials, leading to password reuse and increased attack surface for credential theft.

questions.text: Do you have controlled physical access to your data centers and server rooms?

options.text: Yes, keycard or basic access control

questions.recommendation: Implement multi-factor physical access controls with audit logging for all data center and server room entries, including visitor management.
questions.riskExplanation: Unauthorized physical access can lead to equipment theft, data theft, and sabotage. Physical security is foundational to overall security.

answer.optionText: Yes, keycard or basic access control

questions.text: Do you have video surveillance monitoring critical areas?
questions.recommendation: Deploy video surveillance with adequate retention (90+ days) for all critical areas, with regular review procedures and secure storage.
questions.riskExplanation: Video surveillance deters physical attacks and provides forensic evidence for investigations. Without it, physical incidents are harder to investigate.

questions.text: Do you have visitor management procedures for all facilities?

options.text: Yes, with escort requirements and logging

questions.recommendation: Implement comprehensive visitor management including pre-registration, badge issuance, escort requirements, and exit confirmation.
questions.riskExplanation: Unmanaged visitors pose significant security risks. Formal procedures ensure accountability and prevent unauthorized access.

answer.optionText: Yes, with escort requirements and logging

questions.text: Do you have environmental controls (fire suppression, HVAC, UPS) for critical infrastructure?
questions.recommendation: Implement comprehensive environmental controls with monitoring, regular maintenance, and automated alerts for fire, temperature, humidity, and power.
questions.riskExplanation: Environmental failures (fire, flood, power loss) can cause catastrophic damage and extended downtime. Proper controls are essential for availability.

questions.text: Do you have documented security policies covering all major areas?
questions.recommendation: Develop and maintain a comprehensive set of security policies with annual reviews, including acceptance tracking and compliance monitoring.
questions.riskExplanation: Without clear policies, security practices are inconsistent and employees lack guidance on proper security behaviors.

questions.text: Do you provide regular security awareness training to all employees?
questions.recommendation: Implement quarterly security awareness training with phishing simulations, covering current threats and reinforcing security best practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Employees are often the weakest link. Regular training significantly reduces the risk of phishing, social engineering, and human error.

questions.text: Do you have an incident response plan that is regularly tested?
questions.recommendation: Develop a comprehensive incident response plan with defined roles, playbooks, and conduct annual tabletop exercises to test and improve response capabilities.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a tested incident response plan, security incidents will be handled chaotically, increasing damage and recovery time.

questions.text: Do you conduct regular security compliance audits or assessments?
questions.recommendation: Schedule annual security assessments with qualified auditors to validate compliance with policies, regulations, and industry best practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Without regular audits, security gaps may go undetected, and you may fail to identify non-compliance with regulatory requirements.

questions.text: Do you have a next-generation firewall (NGFW) deployed at your network perimeter?

options.text: Yes, with comprehensive IPS/IDS and application control

questions.recommendation: Deploy a next-generation firewall with intrusion prevention, deep packet inspection, and application-aware filtering to protect your network perimeter.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a modern firewall, your network perimeter is vulnerable to unauthorized access, malware, and sophisticated attacks that can bypass traditional packet filters.

questions.text: Do you use a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect public-facing web applications?
questions.recommendation: Implement a WAF for all public-facing web applications to protect against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, SQL injection, XSS, and other web-based attacks.
questions.riskExplanation: Web applications are common attack vectors. Without WAF protection, your applications are exposed to injection attacks, data breaches, and service disruptions.

questions.text: Do you conduct regular penetration testing of your external-facing infrastructure?
questions.recommendation: Schedule quarterly penetration tests by qualified security professionals to identify and remediate vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.
questions.riskExplanation: Without regular penetration testing, unknown vulnerabilities in your perimeter defenses may remain undetected until exploited by malicious actors.

questions.text: Do you have DDoS protection services in place?

options.text: Yes, with dedicated DDoS mitigation service

questions.recommendation: Implement a dedicated DDoS protection service with traffic scrubbing capabilities to ensure availability during volumetric attacks.
questions.riskExplanation: DDoS attacks can cause significant downtime and revenue loss. Basic ISP protection is often insufficient against sophisticated, multi-vector attacks.

questions.text: Is your internal network segmented to separate critical systems from general traffic?

options.text: Yes, with multiple security zones and strict controls

questions.recommendation: Implement network segmentation using VLANs, subnets, and firewall rules to isolate critical systems and limit lateral movement by attackers.
questions.riskExplanation: Flat networks allow attackers to move freely once they gain initial access. Segmentation contains breaches and protects critical assets.

questions.text: Do you monitor network traffic for security anomalies and intrusions?

options.text: Yes, with SIEM and automated alerting

questions.recommendation: Deploy a SIEM solution with network traffic analysis, anomaly detection, and automated alerting to identify suspicious activities in real-time.
questions.riskExplanation: Without network monitoring, security incidents may go undetected for extended periods, allowing attackers to exfiltrate data or cause damage.

questions.text: Do you enforce network access control (NAC) for devices connecting to your network?
questions.recommendation: Implement 802.1X authentication with NAC to ensure only authorized and compliant devices can access network resources.
questions.riskExplanation: Unauthorized devices on your network can introduce malware, bypass security controls, and provide attackers with entry points.

questions.text: Do you use VPN with multi-factor authentication for remote access?

options.text: Yes, MFA required for all remote users
Yes, MFA optional or for some users

questions.recommendation: Enforce MFA for all VPN connections and consider implementing Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) for more secure remote access.
questions.riskExplanation: VPN credentials are frequently targeted. Without MFA, compromised credentials allow attackers full access to your internal network.

answer.optionText: Yes, MFA optional or for some users

questions.text: Do you have endpoint detection and response (EDR) deployed on all corporate devices?

options.text: Yes, on all devices with centralized management

questions.recommendation: Deploy EDR solutions across all endpoints to detect, investigate, and respond to threats in real-time with automated containment capabilities.
questions.riskExplanation: Endpoints are primary attack vectors. Without EDR, malware and advanced threats can spread undetected across your organization.

answer.optionText: Yes, on all devices with centralized management

questions.text: Are all endpoints kept up-to-date with security patches within a defined timeframe?
questions.recommendation: Implement automated patch management with defined SLAs (e.g., critical patches within 48 hours, all patches within 7 days) to reduce vulnerability exposure.
questions.riskExplanation: Unpatched vulnerabilities are among the most common exploitation methods. Delays in patching increase your risk significantly.

questions.text: Do you enforce full-disk encryption on all corporate laptops and mobile devices?
questions.recommendation: Mandate full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or equivalent) on all corporate devices to protect data at rest in case of theft or loss.
questions.riskExplanation: Unencrypted devices expose sensitive data if lost or stolen. Encryption is a fundamental protection for data at rest.

questions.text: Do you have application whitelisting or allow-listing policies in place?
questions.recommendation: Implement application allow-listing to prevent execution of unauthorized software, reducing the attack surface for malware and unauthorized tools.
questions.riskExplanation: Without application control, users can install malicious or unauthorized software, increasing security risks and compliance issues.

questions.text: Do you conduct static application security testing (SAST) during development?
questions.recommendation: Integrate SAST tools into your CI/CD pipeline to automatically detect security vulnerabilities during the development process.
questions.riskExplanation: Security vulnerabilities introduced during development are expensive to fix later. SAST catches issues early in the lifecycle.

questions.text: Do you perform dynamic application security testing (DAST) on applications before production deployment?
questions.recommendation: Implement automated DAST scanning for all application releases to identify runtime vulnerabilities before they reach production.
questions.riskExplanation: Runtime vulnerabilities are only detectable when applications are running. DAST complements SAST by finding issues in deployed configurations.

questions.text: Do you use software composition analysis (SCA) to scan third-party dependencies?

options.text: Yes, automated scanning of all dependencies

questions.recommendation: Implement SCA tools to automatically scan all third-party dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and license compliance issues.
questions.riskExplanation: Third-party libraries often contain vulnerabilities. SCA helps you identify and update risky dependencies before they can be exploited.

questions.text: Do you have a secure software development lifecycle (SSDLC) policy in place?
questions.recommendation: Develop and enforce a comprehensive SSDLC policy that includes security requirements, threat modeling, code reviews, and developer security training.
questions.riskExplanation: Without a structured SSDLC, security is often an afterthought, leading to vulnerabilities that could have been prevented through proper processes.

questions.text: Do you have a formal data classification policy (e.g., public, internal, confidential, restricted)?
questions.recommendation: Implement a data classification framework with automated labeling and enforce appropriate protection controls based on classification levels.
questions.riskExplanation: Without data classification, you cannot apply appropriate protection controls, leading to either over-protection of low-value data or under-protection of sensitive information.

questions.text: Do you encrypt sensitive data both at rest and in transit?

options.text: Yes, for at rest or transit only

questions.recommendation: Implement strong encryption (AES-256 for at rest, TLS 1.3 for transit) for all sensitive data, with proper key management practices.
questions.riskExplanation: Unencrypted data is vulnerable to interception and theft. Encryption is essential for protecting sensitive information in all states.

questions.text: Do you have regular data backup with tested recovery procedures?

options.text: Yes, automated with quarterly recovery tests
Yes, automated but no regular testing

questions.recommendation: Implement the 3-2-1 backup strategy (3 copies, 2 different media, 1 offsite) with regular recovery testing to ensure business continuity.
questions.riskExplanation: Without tested backups, data loss from ransomware, hardware failure, or human error can be catastrophic and unrecoverable.

answer.optionText: Yes, automated with quarterly recovery tests

questions.text: Do you implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls?

options.text: Yes, with endpoint and network DLP

questions.recommendation: Deploy comprehensive DLP solutions across endpoints, network, and cloud to prevent unauthorized transmission of sensitive data.
questions.riskExplanation: Data breaches often occur through accidental or malicious data exfiltration. DLP controls help prevent sensitive data from leaving your environment.

questions.text: Do you enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all admin accounts?

options.text: Yes, for all admin and privileged accounts

questions.recommendation: Enforce MFA using phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2, hardware keys) for all administrative and privileged accounts without exception.
questions.riskExplanation: Admin accounts are high-value targets. Without MFA, compromised credentials give attackers full control over your systems.

questions.text: Do you enforce MFA for all user accounts?

options.text: Yes, optional or for some users

questions.recommendation: Implement MFA for all user accounts, starting with passwordless authentication where possible, to dramatically reduce credential theft risks.
questions.riskExplanation: Password-based authentication is fundamentally weak. MFA is one of the most effective controls against account compromise.
